log.text: Design: grants and removes job keys; idle guard; end step runs every time, with Slurm's epilog as backup.
Design: generic board lease (kotl lease/run/release); end step kills every PC-account process; no FireSim knowledge in the core.

Lease: start (ownership, license, claim), log, end step (idempotent; epilog backup), watcher guards (--max, --idle) via scancel as Slurm operator; job.sh with a FIFO log pipe; deploy/kotl/install.sh.
Integration run found: the watcher refused itself (inherited SUDO_USER), so --max never tripped. Fixed: watcher starts without SUDO_* variables.

M3: start --pubkey, grant/revoke access, owner-only 'result' and 'put' subcommands.
Exit plan enforced (no time limit = refused; lease always idle-guarded via kotl-keys busy); KOTL RESULT marker read from any command's output; start prints board= and pc= for job.sh.

issues: Soft lockdown: password logins to virtex-host bypass the queue until full lockdown (user's choice for now).

log.text: New part: per-job SSH keys, added at job start and removed by the end step and Slurm's epilog.
Design: end step kills every process of the PC account.
Lab answer: job keys go to virtex-host; Kotl owns its authorized_keys.
Design: lockdown setting, soft now (job's own work only) and full later (kill every virtex-host process).
Design: kotl-keys helper and PC sudoers rule shown as file cards.
Job keys: made by job.sh as the user; launcher validates (bare ssh-ed25519) and adds/removes them via kotl-keys (as virtex-host, sudo from kotl); unreachable PC refuses the start and frees the board.
job.sh gives the command an ssh-agent with only the job key, plus KOTL_JOB/KOTL_BOARD/KOTL_PC; kotl-keys busy for the lease idle guard.
Planned (user goal): Kotl installs and removes its PC side itself (account, key, kotl-keys, sudoers), via kotl/ssh.py, asking the admin's PC password once; replaces the manual scp/ssh steps.
Planned (user goal): one command runs every --undo in reverse and removes the PC side; --purge also packages, data, accounts. Tested: install then uninstall leaves nothing.
